text.p: Following are the highlights of main stories in Serbian and Montenegrin papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
POLITIKA

- Serbia sets up Regional Development Office in Kosovo. Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic calls on Kosovo Albanians to vote at the upcoming Serbian elections demonstrating their readiness to use legal insitutions.
- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutionvic invited OSCE to monitor Serbian September 21 elections.

- Slovenia will protest to the international mediator for the succession of ex-Yugoslavia Sir Arthur Watts over Belgrade plans to include in its privatisation formerly Slovenian companies and property before the division of assets is concluded.
- Foreign investors demand state guarantees, customs and tax facilities, said director of the consulting firm Deloitte & Touche Vladimir Poznanic.
- Yugoslav airline JAT joins Internet.
- Serbia's engine producer Industrija Motora Rakovica (IMR) to export tractors to Egypt worth $11 million within next eight months in two separate deals.
- Yugoslavia sets up accreditation body which will authorise firms to examine product quality and issue quality certificates.
- Confidence in the dinar returning, the number of dinar deposits has grown by one fifth in the first half of 1997, says postal bank Postanska stedionica AD.
- Domestic oil and sugar production will meet the country's needs in the coming year and there will be surplus for exports according to Toda Vasilic of the business community for industrial plants.
- We expect an even more convincing victory at the upcoming elections, says spokesman of the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) Ivica Dacic.
- Serbia's elections will cost the budget 3.5 million German marks.
- Yugoslav army general staff says number of illegal crossings into Yugoslavia from Albania are increasing. It stepped up control in the border strip.
NASA BORBA
- Bosnian Serb constitutional court will decide on Friday on legality of president Biljana Plavsic's decision to disband parliament. Plavsic declined invitation to attend session.
- Over 3,000 pensioners protested in Belgrade over unpaid pensions.
- Employees of Zastava cars surprised by unofficial reports that talks between Zastava and France's Peugot have failed, will demand explanation from management.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Radovan Karadzic will not leave Bosnian Serb Republic, said his wife Ljiljan Zelen-Karadzic.

- Foreign investors are showing increased interest in our country, due to new reform processes, says leading banker Borka Vucic, adding Germany and Italy are interested in privatisation of the state power company EPS.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin Parliament Speaker Svetozar Marovic invited OSCE to monitor October 5 presidential elections.
- The Montenegrin constututional court annulled candidacy of Momir Bulatovic as DPS presidential candidate. Bulatovic will appeal to the federal Constitutional Court.
- Expert team for preparation of parliamentairy elections held its first meeting on Thursday.
MONITOR

- There were three times more articles on Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic than on president Bulatovic in Pobjeda daily last month according to content analysis. In TV evening News the score is four to one in favour of Djukanovic. Bulatovic coverage not negatively coloured.
- Many tobacco smugglers use the rail line Bar-Belgrade and are prime targets of the police, financial and customs inspectors. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
